html:
The conversion of War Jabi, king of Takrur on the middle Senegal River, to Islam in the early 11th century, making Takrur one of the first kingdoms south of the Sahara with a Muslim ruler and Islamic law.

The geographer al-Bakri reports that War Jabi died in 1040 and that his son fought beside the Almoravids. Arab writers later called all West African Muslims Takruri. The valley, later called Futa Toro, became the home of the Haalpulaar people and a seat of Islamic learning, and its clerics made a revolution in 1776, one of the Fula jihads. See also Takrur.
